text: At the cottage a woman told her that this was Missus Scotts house, and a little woman in black, the widows sister, led her into a low kitchen lit by a smoky lamp. <break time="0.8s" /> Em, the widow, sat by the fire with her face swollen and red, and she looked at Laura as if she could not understand why the girl was there at all. <break time="0.8s" /> Laura only wanted to leave the basket and escape, but before she could refuse, the sister led her into the bedroom where the young mans body lay. <break time="0.8s" /> The young man lay fast asleep, so far away that he could not hear them, and his peaceful face seemed to say that all was well. <break time="0.8s" /> While they had been laughing and the band had been playing, this marvel had come to the lane, and garden parties and lace frocks meant nothing to him. <break time="0.8s" /> With a loud childish sob, Laura said, Forgive my hat, and this time, without waiting for Ems sister, she found her way out of the house and past all those dark people. <break time="0.8s" /> At the corner of the lane she met Laurie, whom their anxious mother had sent to find her, and as she pressed close against him, he saw that she was crying. <break time="0.8s" /> When Laurie asked if it had been awful, she sobbed, No, it was simply marvelous, and then she stammered, Is not life, but what life was she could not explain. <break time="0.8s" /> But it did not matter, for Laurie quite understood, and he simply answered, Is it not, darling.
